Since \(A + B + C = \pi\), we get \(A + B = \pi - C\), so \(\cos(A + B) = \cos(\pi - C) = -\cos C\).
L.H.S. \(= (\cos 2A + \cos 2B) + \cos 2C\)
\(= 2\cos(A + B)\cos(A - B) + (2\cos^{2}C - 1)\)
\(= -2\cos C\cos(A - B) + 2\cos^{2}C - 1\)
\(= -1 - 2\cos C\,[\cos(A - B) - \cos C]\)
Using \(\cos C = -\cos(A + B)\) once more,
\(\cos(A - B) - \cos C = \cos(A - B) + \cos(A + B) = 2\cos A\cos B\)
\(\therefore\) L.H.S. \(= -1 - 2\cos C\,(2\cos A\cos B)\)
\(= -1 - 4\cos A\cos B\cos C = \) R.H.S.

Since \(A + B + C = \pi\), we get \(\dfrac{A + B}{2} = \dfrac{\pi}{2} - \dfrac{C}{2}\), so \(\sin\dfrac{A + B}{2} = \cos\dfrac{C}{2}\) and \(\cos\dfrac{A + B}{2} = \sin\dfrac{C}{2}\).
L.H.S. \(= (\sin A + \sin B) + \sin C\)
\(= 2\sin\dfrac{A + B}{2}\cos\dfrac{A - B}{2} + 2\sin\dfrac{C}{2}\cos\dfrac{C}{2}\)
\(= 2\cos\dfrac{C}{2}\cos\dfrac{A - B}{2} + 2\cos\dfrac{C}{2}\cos\dfrac{A + B}{2}\)
\(= 2\cos\dfrac{C}{2}\left[\cos\dfrac{A - B}{2} + \cos\dfrac{A + B}{2}\right]\)
\(= 2\cos\dfrac{C}{2}\left(2\cos\dfrac{A}{2}\cos\dfrac{B}{2}\right)\)
\(= 4\cos\dfrac{A}{2}\cos\dfrac{B}{2}\cos\dfrac{C}{2} = \) R.H.S.

Since \(A + B + C = \pi\), we get \(\dfrac{A + B}{2} = \dfrac{\pi}{2} - \dfrac{C}{2}\), so \(\cos\dfrac{A + B}{2} = \sin\dfrac{C}{2}\).
L.H.S. \(= (\cos A + \cos B) - \cos C\)
\(= 2\cos\dfrac{A + B}{2}\cos\dfrac{A - B}{2} - \left(1 - 2\sin^{2}\dfrac{C}{2}\right)\)
\(= 2\sin\dfrac{C}{2}\cos\dfrac{A - B}{2} - 1 + 2\sin^{2}\dfrac{C}{2}\)
\(= -1 + 2\sin\dfrac{C}{2}\left[\cos\dfrac{A - B}{2} + \sin\dfrac{C}{2}\right]\)
Replacing \(\sin\dfrac{C}{2}\) inside the bracket by \(\cos\dfrac{A + B}{2}\),
\(= -1 + 2\sin\dfrac{C}{2}\left[\cos\dfrac{A - B}{2} + \cos\dfrac{A + B}{2}\right]\)
\(= -1 + 2\sin\dfrac{C}{2}\left(2\cos\dfrac{A}{2}\cos\dfrac{B}{2}\right)\)
\(= 4\cos\dfrac{A}{2}\cos\dfrac{B}{2}\sin\dfrac{C}{2} - 1 = \) R.H.S.

Since \(A + B + C = \pi\), we get \(\cos(A + B) = -\cos C\).
Using \(\sin^{2}\theta = \dfrac{1 - \cos 2\theta}{2}\) on the first two terms and \(\sin^{2}C = 1 - \cos^{2}C\),
L.H.S. \(= 1 - \dfrac{1}{2}(\cos 2A + \cos 2B) + \sin^{2}C\)
\(= 1 - \cos(A + B)\cos(A - B) + 1 - \cos^{2}C\)
\(= 2 + \cos C\cos(A - B) - \cos^{2}C\)
\(= 2 + \cos C\,[\cos(A - B) - \cos C]\)
\(= 2 + \cos C\,[\cos(A - B) + \cos(A + B)]\)
\(= 2 + \cos C\,(2\cos A\cos B)\)
\(= 2 + 2\cos A\cos B\cos C = \) R.H.S.

Since \(A + B + C = \pi\), we get \(\dfrac{A + B}{2} = \dfrac{\pi}{2} - \dfrac{C}{2}\), so \(\cos\dfrac{A + B}{2} = \sin\dfrac{C}{2}\).
Using \(\sin^{2}\dfrac{\theta}{2} = \dfrac{1 - \cos\theta}{2}\) on each term,
L.H.S. \(= \dfrac{1 - \cos A}{2} + \dfrac{1 - \cos B}{2} - \dfrac{1 - \cos C}{2}\)
\(= \dfrac{1}{2} - \dfrac{1}{2}(\cos A + \cos B) + \dfrac{1}{2}\cos C\)
\(= \dfrac{1}{2} - \cos\dfrac{A + B}{2}\cos\dfrac{A - B}{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}\left(1 - 2\sin^{2}\dfrac{C}{2}\right)\)
\(= 1 - \sin\dfrac{C}{2}\cos\dfrac{A - B}{2} - \sin^{2}\dfrac{C}{2}\)
\(= 1 - \sin\dfrac{C}{2}\left[\cos\dfrac{A - B}{2} + \sin\dfrac{C}{2}\right]\)
\(= 1 - \sin\dfrac{C}{2}\left[\cos\dfrac{A - B}{2} + \cos\dfrac{A + B}{2}\right]\)
\(= 1 - \sin\dfrac{C}{2}\left(2\cos\dfrac{A}{2}\cos\dfrac{B}{2}\right)\)
\(= 1 - 2\cos\dfrac{A}{2}\cos\dfrac{B}{2}\sin\dfrac{C}{2} = \) R.H.S.

Since \(A + B + C = \pi\), dividing by \(2\) gives \(\dfrac{A}{2} + \dfrac{B}{2} + \dfrac{C}{2} = \dfrac{\pi}{2}\), so \(\dfrac{A}{2} + \dfrac{B}{2} = \dfrac{\pi}{2} - \dfrac{C}{2}\).
Taking cotangent of both sides,
\(\cot\left(\dfrac{A}{2} + \dfrac{B}{2}\right) = \cot\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} - \dfrac{C}{2}\right) = \tan\dfrac{C}{2} = \dfrac{1}{\cot\dfrac{C}{2}}\)
Using \(\cot(X + Y) = \dfrac{\cot X\cot Y - 1}{\cot X + \cot Y}\) with \(X = \dfrac{A}{2}\), \(Y = \dfrac{B}{2}\),
\(\dfrac{\cot\dfrac{A}{2}\cot\dfrac{B}{2} - 1}{\cot\dfrac{A}{2} + \cot\dfrac{B}{2}} = \dfrac{1}{\cot\dfrac{C}{2}}\)
Cross-multiplying,
\(\cot\dfrac{A}{2}\cot\dfrac{B}{2}\cot\dfrac{C}{2} - \cot\dfrac{C}{2} = \cot\dfrac{A}{2} + \cot\dfrac{B}{2}\)
\(\therefore\ \cot\dfrac{A}{2} + \cot\dfrac{B}{2} + \cot\dfrac{C}{2} = \cot\dfrac{A}{2}\cot\dfrac{B}{2}\cot\dfrac{C}{2} = \) R.H.S.

Since \(A + B + C = \pi\), multiplying by \(2\) gives \(2A + 2B + 2C = 2\pi\), so \(2A + 2B = 2\pi - 2C\).
Taking tangent of both sides,
\(\tan(2A + 2B) = \tan(2\pi - 2C) = -\tan 2C\)
\(\dfrac{\tan 2A + \tan 2B}{1 - \tan 2A\tan 2B} = -\tan 2C\)
\(\tan 2A + \tan 2B = -\tan 2C\,(1 - \tan 2A\tan 2B)\)
\(\tan 2A + \tan 2B = -\tan 2C + \tan 2A\tan 2B\tan 2C\)
\(\therefore\ \tan 2A + \tan 2B + \tan 2C = \tan 2A\,\tan 2B\,\tan 2C = \) R.H.S.

Since \(A + B + C = \pi\), we get \(\cos(A + B) = -\cos C\).
Using \(\cos^{2}\theta = \dfrac{1 + \cos 2\theta}{2}\) on the first two terms,
L.H.S. \(= 1 + \dfrac{1}{2}(\cos 2A + \cos 2B) - \cos^{2}C\)
\(= 1 + \cos(A + B)\cos(A - B) - \cos^{2}C\)
\(= 1 - \cos C\cos(A - B) - \cos^{2}C\)
\(= 1 - \cos C\,[\cos(A - B) + \cos C]\)
Replacing \(\cos C\) inside the bracket by \(-\cos(A + B)\),
\(= 1 - \cos C\,[\cos(A - B) - \cos(A + B)]\)
\(= 1 - \cos C\,(2\sin A\sin B)\)
\(= 1 - 2\sin A\sin B\cos C = \) R.H.S.
